survival-box.title: The Survival Box: When Help Doesn't Show Up
survival-box.intro: The day the cook called in sick. The day the nanny had a family emergency. The day school closed unexpectedly and I had a presentation in 90 minutes. Every help-supported household has these days, and the ones who survive them are the ones who pre-positioned things for exactly this moment. This is what's stocked, prepped, and waiting in our house so when help falls through, everything else doesn't fall apart with it.

The Emergency Shelf: OXO Good Grips POP Container Set (10-piece)
Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat by Samin Nosrat
The 15-Minute Tools: Joyce Chen Original Unlimited Kitchen Scissors
The Kid Distraction Kit: KiwiCo Monthly Subscription (Atlas or Tinker Crate)
The Mom Reset: Protein Bar Sampler Variety Pack (10 Count)
LectroFan High Fidelity White Noise Machine
Alaska Bear Natural Silk Sleep Mask

travel-day.title: The Travel Day Survival Kit (For Kids and the Mom Carrying Them)
travel-day.intro: The 7-hour flight to grandma's. The 4-hour drive to the hotel. The all-day airport delay we didn't plan for. Travel with kids is a logistics problem dressed up as a vacation. After years of overpacking, under packing, and learning the hard way what kids will and won't tolerate at 30,000 feet, this is what we now travel with. Honest, tested in transit, no fluff.

The Plane Bag: Skip Hop Zoo Big Kid Backpack
The Road Trip Kit: Lusso Gear Kids Travel Tray with iPad Holder
Munchkin Brica Magnetic Stick & Play Window Toys
Skip Hop Zoo Spill-Proof Snack Container
AstroAI Portable Tire Inflator Air Compressor
The Beach or Pool Day: Blue Lizard Sensitive Mineral SPF 50 Lotion
UV Skinz UPF 50+ Kids Swim Shirt
The Mom Carry-On: Anker PowerCore 10000 PD Slim Power Bank

lunchbox.title: The 10-Minute Lunchbox: School Day Survival
lunchbox.intro: Lunchboxes are a daily creative writing exercise no one signed up for. After years of 25-minute morning panics, packed-too-much, packed-too-little, and the unbeatable shame of 'you didn't eat your lunch again,' we landed on a system. This is the box, the tools, the food that earned permanent rotation, and the small additions that save the day when the rest of the lunch looks bleak.

The Prep Tools: OXO Good Grips Apple Slicer + Corer
Wilton Mini Cookie Cutter Set (12 piece)
The Backpack Extras: Hydro Flask Kids 12 oz Wide Mouth Bottle
Fit + Fresh Cool Coolers Slim Ice Packs

playdates.title: Playdates, Screens & Group Play
playdates.intro: Three kids over and the parents are in the kitchen. Work spills into the afternoon and the kid needs to be productively bored. This is the playbook for those hours: apps, group games, screen tools, parallel-play gear. Tested in real chaos.

The Playdate Setup: Melissa & Doug Puffy Sticker Activity Set

tech.title: The Tech & Gadgets I Don't Live Without
tech.intro: I work from home. I travel for work. I parent. My tech stack has to do all three. These are the gadgets that earned permanent space in my bag, on my desk, or by my bed. Some unsexy, all essential.

Smart Home & Convenience: Philips Hue White Ambiance Starter Kit

pantry.title: The Pantry Edit: Food, Drink & The Brands I Keep Stocked
pantry.intro: What I actually eat and drink. Not what I serve guests, not what I pack for school. What lives in my fridge, my pantry, my bar cart, and my snack drawer because I genuinely love it. The brands that earn repeat purchases and the food finds that never leave rotation.

The Snack Edit: Kind Bar Dark Chocolate Nuts & Sea Salt

kid-activities.title: Kids Activities That Actually Hold Attention
kid-activities.intro: The activities that actually kept my kids occupied long enough for me to take a meeting, eat in peace, or just sit. Some held attention for 30 minutes. Some for 90. The ones that didn't earn that didn't make this list.
